reasons: Attempt 2 is the one a maintainer is most likely to merge. It keeps the existing set-based algorithm and public behavior, activates only for the all-nodes path, and removes the two real costs in the old inner loop: building set(G._pred[j]) and set(G._succ[j]) again for every incident neighbor of every node, and then counting the four intersections with a Python generator expression. It caches each node's predecessor/successor sets once (as union and reciprocal sets) and counts the same four intersections with len(set & set), doubling only reciprocal neighbors as chain(ipreds, isuccs) did. That is 28 lines, no new imports, no integer-label restriction, no n threshold, and no machinery beyond what appears in the existing set-caching optimization in square_clustering. The bitset candidates are faster, but each either relies on contiguous integer labels, adds an arbitrary node-count cutoff, uses module-level caches or private adjacency traversal in new ways, or is too long and subtle for the speedup over this. The measured 3.25x geometric mean (2.48x–3.91x) is a substantial, low-risk improvement.
